verses.1: And a man went from the house of Levi, and he took the daughter of Levi with him.
verses.2: And the woman became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She saw that he was good, so she breastfed him for three months.
verses.3: And she couldn’t do anything anymore. So she took a piece of cloth, wrapped it around the child, and put him inside that cloth. Then she covered the cloth with a cover.
verses.4: And he placed his brother far away, so that he could know what would happen to him.
verses.5: And Pharaoh’s daughter went out into the field to hunt. Her daughters followed her along with her. They saw a bird inside the nest. Then she sent for her servant and took it away.
verses.6: And she opened her eyes and saw the child. It was a young boy who was crying. She felt sorry for him and said, “Who is this child from among the Israelites?”
verses.7: And his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Go and call a woman from my household. She will give birth to the child for you.”
verses.8: And the daughter of Pharaoh said to her, “Go away.” So she went away into the world and called for the mother of the child.
verses.9: And the daughter of Pharaoh said to her, “I will give this child to you. I will also give you your reward.” Then the woman took the child and breastfed him.
verses.10: And the child grew up. His mother brought him before Pharaoh’s daughter, and she became his mother. She named him Moses. She said, “He was born from the water.”
verses.11: And in those days, Moses grew up and went to his brothers. He saw their suffering, and he saw that a Egyptian was killing one of his brothers.
verses.12: And he did this and that. He saw that there was no one there. So he destroyed the Egyptian and buried him in the ground.
verses.13: On the second day, two Israelites were walking along the road. The wicked man said to him, “Why do you hate your friend?”
verses.14: And he said, “Who has appointed you to be a ruler and judge over us? You said that you would kill the Egyptians. Moses was afraid, and he said, ‘Now I know what it means.’”
verses.15: Pharaoh heard this and wanted to kill Moses. But Moses ran away from Pharaoh. He settled in the land of Midian, and he lived on the banks of the river.
verses.16: And the priest from Midian had seven daughters. They came, brought them forward, and filled the vessels with milk for feeding the sheep of their father.
verses.17: And the wicked came and drove them away. But Moses stood up and saved them, and he comforted their souls.
verses.18: And she went to her father Reuvel. He said, “Why do you come here today?”
verses.19: And they said, “The Egyptians saved us from the hands of the enemies. They also gave us food in plenty.”
verses.20: And he said to his daughters, “Why have you left this man? He needs someone who will feed him with bread.”
verses.21: And Moses asked the man to sit down. Then he gave his wife to Moses as a gift.
verses.22: And he had a son. He named him Gershom, because he said, “Gershom, I was born in a foreign land.”
verses.23: And in those many years, the king of Egypt died. Then the children of Israel mourned for their master. They cried out in sorrow, and their grief turned towards God from their slavery.
verses.24: And God heard their prayers. He remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.25: And God saw the children of Israel, and He knew them.
